description: Fix the service worker reload loop that causes dashboard state to revert. The sw.js calls skipWaiting() on install and sends SW_UPDATED to all clients, while main.js listens for controllerchange and SW_UPDATED messages and calls window.location.reload() on both. This creates a reload cycle that resets in-memory auth state (JWT token) and connector status after connecting integrations.
steps: In dashboard/sw.js: Remove the self.skipWaiting() call from the install event handler. The activate event should only purge old caches and claim clients without sending SW_UPDATED immediately. Instead, let the new SW wait until the user navigates away or the app explicitly triggers the update.

In dashboard/main.js: Remove the aggressive controllerchange event listener that calls window.location.reload(). Remove the SW_UPDATED message listener that also calls window.location.reload(). Remove the interval that calls reg.update() every 60 seconds. Remove the code that messages reg.waiting with SKIP_WAITING. Instead, implement a non-disruptive update notification: when an updatefound event fires and the new worker reaches 'installed' state, show a subtle toast or banner saying 'Update available - click to refresh' and only reload when the user clicks it.
In dashboard/sw.js activate handler: Remove the self.clients.matchAll().then(clients => clients.forEach(client => client.postMessage({ type: 'SW_UPDATED' }))) code. Keep the cache purge logic.
Verify that after these changes, connecting a Shopify or GitHub integration no longer causes the page to reload and lose the connected state.
acceptance_criteria: The service worker no longer calls self.skipWaiting() on install
The activate event no longer sends SW_UPDATED messages to clients
main.js no longer has automatic window.location.reload() calls in the service worker section
The SW registration section in main.js shows a user-initiated refresh pattern instead of forced reload
